title: Migrate perf harness to async runners and stable seeding
creator: Avery Patel
description: Tech debt refactor: replace the legacy synchronous load/perf runners with a unified asyncio-based runner abstraction, introduce deterministic seeding for synthetic generators, and simplify workload bucketization. Goals: reduce flakiness in CI/regression runs, speed up end-to-end eval time by ~25%, and make the harness easier to extend for GPU/CPU runtime variants. This ticket covers code changes, dependency upgrades (pytest-asyncio, aiohttp, upgrade locust plugin), CI adjustments, and adding smoke-canary tests that run in PR gating.
acceptance_criteria: New async runner implemented and selectable via --runner=async or RUNNER=async env
All perf regression CI jobs pass on a clean master for 5 consecutive runs without transient failures
Synthetic workload generators support a --seed flag and runs are reproducible across local and CI (same seed + same model variant => identical request traces)
End-to-end runtime for standard 1k request regression reduced by >=20% measured on the baseline lane
Migration documented in Confluence and playbook updated with steps to revert to legacy runner if needed
A minimal canary smoke job is added to PR gating (linux-small) and a dashboard tile tracks pass rate and median latency of the smoke suite
plan: Spike (2d): prototype asyncio runner for a single scenario to validate KV cache integration and stream handling
Implementation (5d): replace sync runner implementation, add stable-seed support to synthetic generator and scenario manifests
CI work (2d): update GitHub Actions / Kubernetes job templates, add smoke-canary gating job
Rollout (2d): feature-flag default to legacy runner, enable async runner for nightly and a subset of regression lanes; monitor for 72h
Cleanup (2d): flip default when stable, remove deprecated sync code paths and update docs
risks: Async semantics may surface rare race conditions with KV cache eviction logic — needs careful instrumentation
Upgrading test dependencies could introduce incompatibilities with older agents still used by Dedicated replica runs
Short-term CI instability while both runners coexist and teams adapt scenario manifests
Performance regressions for very short sequences (where sync path had optimized micro-batching) — require microbench safeguards
